bull.b: The sharp move to positive earnings and strong operating margins indicates that Protalix can currently convert commercial revenue into meaningful profit. If product sales remain durable, this improved earnings base can support internal funding, strengthen resilience, and reduce dependence on external financing.

A sizeable cash position combined with no debt or warrants gives Protalix greater flexibility to fund operations, advance PRX-115, and manage volatility in commercial receipts. The absence of debt also limits fixed financial obligations and preserves strategic options over the next several quarters.

Growing Elfabrio sales and broader dosing and geographic approvals can expand access to the Fabry treatment market and reinforce the product’s commercial position. Continued regulatory progress also supports partner-led penetration and creates a foundation for recurring product revenue.

bear.b: Dependence on Chiesi purchasing patterns means reported revenue may fluctuate even when underlying demand is unchanged. Uneven shipments and inventory decisions make forecasting less reliable, complicate resource planning, and could weaken the durability of recent growth across coming quarters.

The milestone materially boosted first-half results but is not expected to recur on the same basis. Comparisons that include this payment may overstate the underlying pace of product revenue and profitability, raising the risk that future reported performance normalizes below recent levels.

High observed antibody incidence and unresolved dosing choices could complicate PRX-115 development, including efficacy, infusion-reaction management, trial timing, and eventual positioning. These uncertainties may delay value creation from the pipeline and increase the risk of an unfavorable development outcome.
